newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Intel chief sees Indonesia Internet boom.
newsitem.headline: Intel chief sees Indonesia Internet boom.

text.p: Growth in the number of Indonesians using the Internet could expand above predictions if advertisers and local language products enter the world wide web, Intel Corporation executives said on Tuesday.

Intel President Craig Barrett said after a company presentation in Jakarta that he thought the figure of 200,000 Indonesians using the Internet by the year 2000 was "conservative" for the country of more than 200 million people.
Barrett referred to an industry survey as saying the number of Internet subscribers would exceed 50,000 in 1997 and increase at a rate of 70 percent per annum to more than 250,000 by 2001.
"If the number today is probably 50,000 and sales of computers are around 500,000 a year then it would not surprise me if it was not higher," he told a news conference.
Barrett said the key to expansion of the Internet, which he said is predicted to have around 200 million users by 1999, was the rate at which advertisers entered the world wide web.
"If advertising is increased expontentially, then I expect usage to increase exponentially," he said.

Intel's general manager for the Asia-Pacific, Sean Maloney, told the news conference that more content in languages other than English was also an important factor in increasing Internet usage in the region.
"We have noticed a rapid increase in the number of hits on sites using Asian languages," he said.
Barrett noted that anything that increased the sales of computers was good for Intel, the world's largest computer chip maker.
